subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A student heats 2.00 g of magnesium ribbon strongly in an open crucible until it has all been converted to a white solid, MgO. The white solid has a mass of 3.32 g. Which statement best explains the mass change?

choices.t: Mass is not conserved in this reaction because energy was released as heat and light.
Magnesium atoms became heavier when they turned into Mg²⁺ ions, because an ion has more mass than its atom.
Water vapor from the air condensed onto the hot crucible, and its mass accounts for the 1.32 g gain.
Oxygen gas from the air combined with the magnesium, and the 1.32 g gain is the mass of oxygen that reacted, so the total mass of matter is conserved.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A student heats 6.18 g of green copper(II) carbonate, CuCO3, in an open crucible. It turns into black copper(II) oxide, CuO, with a mass of 3.98 g. Which statement best explains the mass decrease?

choices.t: A gas, CO2, formed and escaped into the air, and its mass is the 2.20 g difference.
Mass was destroyed when the bonds in CuCO3 were broken.
The heat from the burner carried away mass equal to the 2.20 g difference.
Copper atoms evaporated from the crucible while it was heated.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A student burns 1.12 g of iron wool in air and collects 1.60 g of rust-colored Fe2O3. Which statement is consistent with the law of conservation of mass?

choices.t: The product contains 0.48 g of oxygen that came from the air, so the mass of iron plus the mass of oxygen that reacted equals the mass of Fe2O3.
Iron atoms were converted into heavier atoms when the iron was heated, which raised the mass by 0.48 g.
The heat added 0.48 g of mass to the iron, which is why the product weighs more than the reactant.
Conservation of mass applies only to closed containers, so the extra 0.48 g in the open crucible is not accounted for by any reactant.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A student places 2.10 g of NaHCO3 and an excess of vinegar in an open flask on a balance. As the CO2 bubbles away, the balance reading falls by 1.10 g. If the same reaction were run in a sealed, rigid flask on the same balance, what change in balance reading would be observed?

choices.t: A decrease of 1.10 g, the same as in the open flask.
A decrease of 1.10 g, because gases have no mass and the CO2 does not count.
No change, because the CO2 stays inside the flask and the total mass of everything on the balance is conserved.
An increase of 1.10 g, because the trapped gas adds to the mass.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Ethanol, C2H5OH, burns completely in excess oxygen to form only carbon dioxide and water. Which equation, written with the smallest whole-number coefficients, correctly represents this reaction?

choices.t: C2H5OH + 2 O2 → 2 CO + 3 H2O
C2H5OH + 2 O2 → 2 CO2 + 3 H2O
C2H5OH + 3 O2 → 2 CO2 + 3 H2O
C2H5OH + 3 O2 → 2 CO2 + 3 H2O2

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Methanol, CH3OH, burns completely in excess oxygen to form only CO2 and H2O. Which equation, written with the smallest whole-number coefficients, is correct?

choices.t: CH3OH + O2 → CO2 + 2 H2O
2 CH3OH + 2 O2 → 2 CO + 4 H2O
2 CH3OH + 3 O2 → 2 CO2 + 4 H2O
CH3OH + 2 O2 → CO2 + 2 H2O

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Ethane, C2H6, burns completely in excess oxygen to form only CO2 and H2O. Which equation, written with the smallest whole-number coefficients, is correct?

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Glucose, C6H12O6, is oxidized completely in the body to form only CO2 and H2O. Which equation, written with the smallest whole-number coefficients, is correct?

choices.t: C6H12O6 + 3 O2 → 6 CO + 6 H2O

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Aqueous Ba(OH)2 and aqueous CuSO4 are mixed. Both BaSO4 and Cu(OH)2 are insoluble in water. Which is the net ionic equation for the reaction?

choices.t: Ba²⁺(aq) + SO4²⁻(aq) → BaSO4(s)
Cu²⁺(aq) + 2 OH⁻(aq) → Cu(OH)2(s)
Ba(OH)2(aq) + CuSO4(aq) → BaSO4(s) + Cu(OH)2(s)
Ba²⁺(aq) + 2 OH⁻(aq) + Cu²⁺(aq) + SO4²⁻(aq) → BaSO4(s) + Cu(OH)2(s)

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Aqueous Ba(OH)2 and aqueous Fe2(SO4)3 are mixed. Both BaSO4 and Fe(OH)3 are insoluble. Which is the net ionic equation?

choices.t: 3 Ba²⁺(aq) + 3 SO4²⁻(aq) → 3 BaSO4(s)
Ba²⁺(aq) + 2 OH⁻(aq) + Fe³⁺(aq) + SO4²⁻(aq) → BaSO4(s) + Fe(OH)3(s)
3 Ba²⁺(aq) + 6 OH⁻(aq) + 2 Fe³⁺(aq) + 3 SO4²⁻(aq) → 3 BaSO4(s) + 2 Fe(OH)3(s)
2 Fe³⁺(aq) + 6 OH⁻(aq) → 2 Fe(OH)3(s)

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Aqueous Pb(NO3)2 and aqueous KI are mixed, and yellow solid PbI2 forms. KNO3 is soluble. Which is the net ionic equation?

choices.t: Pb²⁺(aq) + I⁻(aq) → PbI(s)
Pb(NO3)2(aq) + 2 KI(aq) → PbI2(s) + 2 KNO3(aq)
Pb²⁺(aq) + 2 NO3⁻(aq) + 2 K⁺(aq) + 2 I⁻(aq) → PbI2(s) + 2 K⁺(aq) + 2 NO3⁻(aq)
Pb²⁺(aq) + 2 I⁻(aq) → PbI2(s)

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Aqueous KI and aqueous NaNO3 are mixed. Both possible products, KNO3 and NaI, are soluble. Which statement is correct?

choices.t: K⁺(aq) + NO3⁻(aq) → KNO3(s) is the net ionic equation.
Na⁺(aq) + I⁻(aq) → NaI(s) is the net ionic equation.
A reaction occurs because the molecular equation KI + NaNO3 → KNO3 + NaI can be written.
All four ions stay dissolved and are spectators, so there is no net ionic equation.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Aqueous acetic acid, HC2H3O2, a weak acid, is mixed with aqueous sodium hydroxide. Which is the net ionic equation for the reaction?

choices.t: HC2H3O2(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → C2H3O2⁻(aq) + H2O(l)
H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H2O(l)
HC2H3O2(aq) + Na⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → Na⁺(aq) + C2H3O2⁻(aq) + H2O(l)
HC2H3O2(aq) + NaOH(aq) → NaC2H3O2(aq) + H2O(l)

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Aqueous hydrofluoric acid, HF, a weak acid, is mixed with aqueous potassium hydroxide. Which is the net ionic equation?

choices.t: H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H2O(l)
HF(aq) + K⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → K⁺(aq) + F⁻(aq) + H2O(l)
HF(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → F⁻(aq) + H2O(l)
HF(aq) + KOH(aq) → KF(aq) + H2O(l)

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Aqueous ammonia, NH3, a weak base, is mixed with aqueous hydrochloric acid. Which is the net ionic equation?

choices.t: H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H2O(l)
NH3(aq) + H⁺(aq) → NH4⁺(aq)
NH4⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) → NH4Cl(s)
NH3(aq) + H⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) → NH4⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq)

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Solid Mg(OH)2, which is essentially insoluble in water, dissolves in aqueous HCl. Which is the net ionic equation?

choices.t: Mg(OH)2(s) + 2 H⁺(aq) → Mg²⁺(aq) + 2 H2O(l)
H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H2O(l)
Mg²⁺(aq) + 2 Cl⁻(aq) → MgCl2(s)
Mg(OH)2(s) + 2 H⁺(aq) + 2 Cl⁻(aq) → Mg²⁺(aq) + 2 Cl⁻(aq) + 2 H2O(l)

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A particle drawing of the reactant mixture shows 3 N2 molecules and 6 H2 molecules in a sealed container. The reaction N2 + 3 H2 → 2 NH3 then goes to completion. Which description of the final mixture is correct?

choices.t: 4 NH3 molecules and 1 N2 molecule
6 NH3 molecules and nothing else
6 NH3 molecules and 3 H2 molecules
4 NH3 molecules and 2 N2 molecules

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A particle drawing of the reactant mixture shows 6 H2 molecules and 4 O2 molecules in a sealed container. The reaction 2 H2 + O2 → 2 H2O then goes to completion. Which description of the final mixture is correct?

choices.t: 8 H2O molecules
6 H2O molecules and 1 O2 molecule
6 H2O molecules and 3 O2 molecules
6 H2O molecules and 2 O2 molecules

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A particle drawing of the reactant mixture shows 3 CH4 molecules and 4 O2 molecules in a sealed container. The reaction CH4 + 2 O2 → CO2 + 2 H2O then goes to completion. Which description of the final mixture is correct?

choices.t: 2 CO2 molecules, 4 H2O molecules and 1 CH4 molecule
3 CO2 molecules and 6 H2O molecules
2 CO2 molecules, 4 H2O molecules and 2 CH4 molecules
2 CO2 molecules, 2 H2O molecules and 1 CH4 molecule

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A particle drawing of the reactant mixture shows 6 SO2 molecules and 5 O2 molecules in a sealed container. The reaction 2 SO2 + O2 → 2 SO3 then goes to completion. Which description of the final mixture is correct?

choices.t: 6 SO3 molecules and no other molecules
6 SO3 molecules and 4 O2 molecules
6 SO3 molecules and 5 O2 molecules
6 SO3 molecules and 2 O2 molecules

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A sealed, rigid container holds 4 H2 molecules and 2 O2 molecules. They react completely according to 2 H2 + O2 → 2 H2O. Which statement correctly compares the contents before and after the reaction?

choices.t: The total number of molecules and the total mass are the same, but the number of atoms changes.
The total number of molecules and the total number of atoms are the same, but the total mass changes.
The number of molecules, the number of atoms of each element and the total mass all change because a new substance forms.
The total number of atoms of each element and the total mass are the same, but the number of molecules changes from 6 to 4.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A rigid container at constant temperature holds 4 CO molecules and 2 O2 molecules at a pressure P0. They react completely according to 2 CO + O2 → 2 CO2. What is the pressure after the reaction, if all species are gases?

choices.t: P0, because mass and atoms are conserved.
1.5 P0, because 4 CO2 molecules are formed from the reactants.
(2/3) P0, because the number of gas molecules falls from 6 to 4.
(1/2) P0, because the 2 O2 molecules and 2 of the CO molecules disappear.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A sealed rigid container holds 6 H2O2 molecules, which decompose completely according to 2 H2O2 → 2 H2O + O2. Which statement about the contents after the reaction is correct?

choices.t: There are 6 molecules, because the number of molecules is conserved in a reaction.
There are 9 molecules and the total number of atoms is 24, unchanged.
There are 9 molecules and the total number of atoms is 30.
There are 12 molecules, because each H2O2 gives one H2O and one O2.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A beaker holds a solution with 5 Ag⁺, 5 NO3⁻, 3 Na⁺ and 3 Cl⁻ ions (represented as particles). AgCl is insoluble and NaNO3 is soluble. Which description of the mixture after the precipitation is correct?

choices.t: 5 AgCl(s) with 3 Na⁺ and 5 NO3⁻ in solution
3 AgCl(s) with 2 Ag⁺, 3 Na⁺ and 5 NO3⁻ in solution
3 AgCl(s) with 2 Ag⁺, 3 Na⁺ and 2 NO3⁻ in solution
3 AgCl(s), 3 NaNO3(s), and 2 Ag⁺ and 2 NO3⁻ in solution

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A student records four separate observations. Which one is the strongest evidence that a chemical change occurred?

choices.t: White crystals stirred into water disappear, and the temperature of the water drops by 3°C.
A colorless liquid is heated to boiling; the vapor is condensed, and the collected liquid has the same boiling point as the original liquid.
A blue solid melts to a deep blue liquid at 110°C and solidifies back to the same blue solid when cooled.
A shiny gray metal ribbon burns in air with a bright white flame, leaving a white powder that is heavier than the ribbon and does not conduct electricity.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A student heats a white solid and records the observations below. Which observation, if made, would show that a chemical change occurred?

choices.t: The heated solid releases a gas that turns limewater cloudy, and the residue has a different melting point and a lower mass than the original solid.
The solid melts at 80°C, and the cooled liquid solidifies to a white solid that again melts at 80°C.
The solid dissolves in water, and after the water evaporates the recovered solid has the same mass and the same melting point as before.
The solid sublimes onto a cold surface as crystals that have the same melting point as the original solid.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Which process involves breaking covalent bonds within molecules, and is therefore a chemical change?

choices.t: Heating sugar until it chars into black carbon and water vapor
Dissolving sugar in water so the sucrose molecules separate from one another
Boiling water to steam
Melting an ice cube

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A student tests four trials on a 5.00 g sample of a white solid with a melting point of 63°C. Which trial describes only a physical change?

choices.t: After heating in a sealed tube, the mass is still 5.00 g, but the solid now melts at 120°C.
After dissolving the solid in water and evaporating the water, 5.00 g of white solid is recovered, and it melts at 63°C.
After heating, 1.20 g of an odorous gas is released, and the remaining solid melts at 90°C.
After mixing with a clear liquid, a bright yellow solid forms that melts at 98°C.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: The energy needed to vaporize 1 mol of H2O(l) at 25°C is 44 kJ. The energy needed to decompose 1 mol of H2O(g) into H2(g) and 1/2 O2(g) is 242 kJ. Which statement best interprets these data?

choices.t: Vaporization breaks some of the O-H bonds in water, but decomposition breaks every one of them, which takes more energy.
Vaporization only overcomes intermolecular forces between intact molecules, while decomposition breaks strong covalent O-H bonds and forms new substances.
Decomposition needs more energy because the molecules in a gas are farther apart than in a liquid.
Decomposition must also overcome the hydrogen bonds in the liquid, so it needs the vaporization energy plus extra energy.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: The energy needed to sublime 1 mol of CO2(s) is about 25 kJ. The energy needed to decompose 1 mol of CO2(g) into C(s) and O2(g) is about 394 kJ. Which statement best interprets these data?

choices.t: Sublimation breaks C=O bonds in each molecule, but fewer of them than decomposition.
Decomposition needs more energy because solid CO2 has stronger intermolecular forces than gaseous CO2.
Both processes break covalent bonds, and the difference is only in how many bonds break.
Sublimation overcomes weak attractions between intact CO2 molecules, but decomposition breaks the C=O bonds within molecules.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: The energy needed to melt 1 mol of NaCl(s) is about 28 kJ. The energy needed to convert 1 mol of NaCl(s) into Na(s) and 1/2 Cl2(g) is about 411 kJ. Which statement best interprets these data?

choices.t: Melting converts Na⁺ ions to Na atoms, but only partly, so less energy is needed than for complete conversion.
Melting loosens the lattice but leaves Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions in the same substance, while the second process changes the ions into Na atoms and Cl2 molecules.
Both processes produce new substances, and the larger energy change is due to producing a gas.
Melting breaks every ionic bond completely, so the second process must be breaking something else, such as nuclei.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: The energy needed to sublime 1 mol of I2(s) is about 62 kJ. The energy needed to dissociate 1 mol of I2(g) into 2 I(g) is about 151 kJ. Which statement best interprets these data?

choices.t: Sublimation is a chemical change because it needs a large amount of energy.
Sublimation overcomes dispersion forces between intact I2 molecules, while dissociation breaks the I-I covalent bond and forms different particles.
Both processes break I-I bonds, and dissociation requires more energy because the bonds are stronger in the gas.
Dissociation is a physical change because the iodine remains iodine.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Aluminum reacts with chlorine according to 2 Al + 3 Cl2 → 2 AlCl3. A student mixes 5.40 g of Al (26.98 g/mol) with 10.65 g of Cl2 (70.90 g/mol) and collects 11.2 g of AlCl3 (133.33 g/mol). What is the percent yield?

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Ammonia reacts with oxygen according to 4 NH3 + 5 O2 → 4 NO + 6 H2O. A student mixes 8.50 g of NH3 (17.03 g/mol) with 16.0 g of O2 (32.00 g/mol) and collects 9.60 g of NO (30.01 g/mol). What is the percent yield?

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: In the thermite reaction Fe2O3 + 2 Al → Al2O3 + 2 Fe, a student mixes 16.0 g of Fe2O3 (159.69 g/mol) with 4.05 g of Al (26.98 g/mol) and obtains 6.70 g of Fe (55.85 g/mol). What is the percent yield of iron?

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Hydrogen burns in oxygen according to 2 H2 + O2 → 2 H2O. A student mixes 3.00 g of H2 (2.016 g/mol) with 20.0 g of O2 (32.00 g/mol) and collects 19.4 g of H2O (18.02 g/mol). What is the percent yield?

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: An impure 5.00 g sample of KClO3 (122.55 g/mol) is heated until it decomposes completely according to 2 KClO3 → 2 KCl + 3 O2. The impurities do not release any gas. The O2 produced has a mass of 1.20 g (32.00 g/mol). What is the mass percent of KClO3 in the sample?

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: An impure 2.25 g sample of aluminum reacts with excess HCl according to 2 Al + 6 HCl → 2 AlCl3 + 3 H2. The impurities do not react. The H2 produced has a mass of 0.150 g (2.016 g/mol). What is the mass percent of Al (26.98 g/mol) in the sample?

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: An impure 4.20 g sample of NaHCO3 (84.01 g/mol) is heated according to 2 NaHCO3 → Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2. The impurities do not release gas. The CO2 produced has a mass of 0.880 g (44.01 g/mol). What is the mass percent of NaHCO3 in the sample?

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Hydrogen peroxide solution decomposes according to 2 H2O2 → 2 H2O + O2. A 10.00 g sample of the solution produces 0.141 g of O2 (32.00 g/mol). What is the mass percent of H2O2 (34.01 g/mol) in the solution?

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A 25.00 mL sample of H2SO4(aq) is titrated to the equivalence point with 0.2000 M NaOH(aq), which requires 30.00 mL. The reaction is H2SO4 + 2 NaOH → Na2SO4 + 2 H2O. What is the concentration of the H2SO4 solution?

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A 20.00 mL sample of Ba(OH)2(aq) is titrated to the equivalence point with 0.1500 M HCl(aq), which requires 28.40 mL. The reaction is Ba(OH)2 + 2 HCl → BaCl2 + 2 H2O. What is the concentration of the Ba(OH)2 solution?

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A 25.00 mL sample of H3PO4(aq) is titrated with 0.1000 M NaOH(aq) until both of the first two protons have been neutralized, forming Na2HPO4. This requires 37.50 mL of NaOH. What is the concentration of the H3PO4 solution?

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A 10.00 mL sample of vinegar is diluted to 100.0 mL with water. A 25.00 mL portion of the diluted solution is titrated to the equivalence point with 0.1000 M NaOH, which requires 21.40 mL. The reaction is HC2H3O2 + NaOH → NaC2H3O2 + H2O. What is the concentration of acetic acid in the original, undiluted vinegar?

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A student titrates 25.00 mL of HCl of unknown concentration with standard 0.100 M NaOH from a buret. Before filling, the student rinses the buret with distilled water and leaves the water droplets in it. The titration is otherwise done correctly, and the equivalence point is detected correctly. The student calculates the HCl concentration using 0.100 M for the NaOH. How will the calculated HCl concentration compare with the true value?

choices.t: It will be too low, because the water neutralizes some of the acid.
It will be correct, because water does not contain any acid or base.
It will be too high, because the diluted NaOH has a lower concentration than 0.100 M, so more volume is needed and the calculation overestimates the moles of base.
It will be too low, because less NaOH is needed to reach the equivalence point.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A student titrates 25.00 mL of HCl with 0.100 M NaOH. The tip of the buret contains an air bubble before the titration, and the bubble is expelled during the titration. The initial buret reading is taken with the bubble present. How will the calculated HCl concentration compare with the true value?

choices.t: It will be too low, because the bubble reduces the volume of NaOH delivered.
It will be too high, because the volume difference read from the buret includes the volume the bubble occupied, which is more than the liquid delivered.
It will be correct, because the bubble contains no NaOH and does not change the reaction.
It will be too low, because the bubble makes the endpoint appear earlier.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A student pipets 25.00 mL of HCl into a flask that was rinsed with distilled water and is still wet. The student then titrates with standardized 0.100 M NaOH, using phenolphthalein. How will the calculated HCl concentration compare with the true value?

choices.t: It will be too low, because the added water dilutes the acid.
It will be too high, because more NaOH is needed to neutralize the water.
It will be too low, because the water makes the indicator change color early.
It will be correct, because the water changes the concentration but not the moles of HCl, and the moles are what the NaOH neutralizes.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A student rinses the pipet with distilled water and does not rinse it with the HCl sample before pipetting 25.00 mL of the HCl for titration with 0.100 M NaOH. How will the calculated HCl concentration compare with the true value?

choices.t: It will be too high, because the water adds volume that needs to be neutralized.
It will be correct, because the pipet still delivers 25.00 mL.
It will be too low, because the sample in the pipet is diluted by the water, so it delivers fewer moles of HCl and requires less NaOH.
It will be too high, because the extra water increases the pH at the equivalence point.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A zinc strip is placed in blue CuSO4(aq). Over time, the strip becomes coated with a reddish-brown solid and the blue color fades. Which classification best describes the reaction?

choices.t: Synthesis, because zinc and copper combine into one product.
Double replacement, because the ions swap partners to form an insoluble solid.
Single replacement and redox, because Zn loses electrons and Cu²⁺ gains them to form Cu(s).
Decomposition, because the blue CuSO4 breaks down into simpler substances.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Colorless Na2CO3(aq) is mixed with colorless CaCl2(aq). A cloudy white solid forms, with no gas, no flame and no color change, and no element changes its oxidation number. Which classification best describes the reaction?

choices.t: Double replacement (precipitation), which is not a redox reaction.
Single replacement, because Ca replaces Na in the compound.
Combustion, because a new substance forms and energy is released.
Single replacement and redox, because a solid forms.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A white solid is heated and releases a gas that relights a glowing splint. The solid left behind is KCl. The reaction is 2 KClO3 → 2 KCl + 3 O2. Which classification is best?

choices.t: Synthesis, because a gas is formed.
Decomposition, but not redox, because only one reactant is involved.
Decomposition and redox, because Cl goes from +5 to -1 and O goes from -2 to 0.
Single replacement, because chlorine is replaced by oxygen.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Magnesium ribbon is added to dilute HCl(aq). Bubbles of H2 gas form and the ribbon disappears. Which classification best describes the reaction Mg + 2 HCl → MgCl2 + H2?

choices.t: Acid-base neutralization, because HCl is an acid.
Single replacement and redox, because Mg is oxidized and H⁺ is reduced.
Double replacement, because Mg²⁺ and H⁺ swap anions.
Decomposition, because HCl breaks down into H2.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Which reaction is a synthesis (combination) reaction that is NOT an oxidation-reduction reaction?

choices.t: 2 Mg + O2 → 2 MgO
CaO + CO2 → CaCO3
CaCO3 → CaO + CO2

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Which reaction is a decomposition reaction that is also an oxidation-reduction reaction?

choices.t: CaCO3 → CaO + CO2
Mg(OH)2 → MgO + H2O
2 KClO3 → 2 KCl + 3 O2
NH4Cl → NH3 + HCl

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Which reaction is a synthesis reaction that is also an oxidation-reduction reaction?

choices.t: SO3 + H2O → H2SO4
NH3 + HCl → NH4Cl
Na2O + H2O → 2 NaOH

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Which reaction is NOT an oxidation-reduction reaction?

choices.t: Cl2 + 2 KBr → 2 KCl + Br2
Fe + CuSO4 → FeSO4 + Cu
Mg + 2 HCl → MgCl2 + H2
BaCl2 + Na2SO4 → BaSO4 + 2 NaCl

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Consider the reactions of hydrogencarbonate ion, HCO3⁻, with aqueous NaOH and with aqueous HCl. Which statement correctly describes the role of HCO3⁻ in these reactions?

choices.t: It is an acid in both reactions, because it contains a hydrogen atom.
It acts as an acid with OH⁻ (donating H⁺ to form CO3²⁻) and as a base with H3O⁺ (accepting H⁺ to form H2CO3).
It is a base in both reactions, because it carries a negative charge.
It acts as a base with OH⁻ (accepting H⁺) and as an acid with H3O⁺ (donating H⁺).

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Which pair gives the products formed when HPO4²⁻ reacts with OH⁻ and with H3O⁺, respectively?

choices.t: H2PO4⁻ with OH⁻, and PO4³⁻ with H3O⁺
H2PO4⁻ with both OH⁻ and H3O⁺
PO4³⁻ with OH⁻, and H3PO4 with H3O⁺
PO4³⁻ with OH⁻, and H2PO4⁻ with H3O⁺

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Water reacts with NH3 and, separately, with HF. Which statement correctly describes the role of H2O in these two reactions?

choices.t: It is an acid with NH3 (forming NH4⁺ and OH⁻) and a base with HF (forming H3O⁺ and F⁻).
It is a base with NH3 and an acid with HF.
It is an acid in both reactions, because it contains hydrogen.
It is neither, because water is neutral and does not transfer protons.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: In the reaction HS⁻ + NH4⁺ → H2S + NH3, which two pairs are the conjugate acid-base pairs?

choices.t: HS⁻ / NH4⁺ and H2S / NH3
HS⁻ / NH3 and H2S / NH4⁺
H2S / HS⁻ and NH4⁺ / NH3
H2S / S²⁻ and NH4⁺ / NH3

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Two flasks each contain 25.0 mL of 0.100 M acid. Flask 1 holds HCl, a strong acid, and flask 2 holds CH3COOH, a weak acid. Each is titrated with 0.100 M NaOH to its equivalence point. Which statement compares the volumes of NaOH required?

choices.t: Both need 25.0 mL, because the flasks contain equal moles of acid, and the un-ionized CH3COOH reacts as the NaOH removes the H⁺ that has formed.
Flask 1 needs more NaOH, because HCl produces more H⁺ in solution.
Flask 2 needs less NaOH, because only the small fraction of CH3COOH that is ionized can be neutralized.
Flask 2 needs more NaOH, because a weak acid is harder to neutralize.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Which sample requires more 0.100 M NaOH to reach its equivalence point: 100.0 mL of 0.100 M HCl or 50.0 mL of 0.300 M CH3COOH?

choices.t: The CH3COOH, because it contains 15.0 mmol of acid and the HCl contains only 10.0 mmol.
The HCl, because it is a strong acid.
Both need the same volume, because each acid reacts 1:1 with NaOH.
The HCl, because its volume is larger.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: Two 25.0 mL samples, one of 0.100 M HCl and one of 0.100 M H2SO4, are each titrated with 0.100 M NaOH until both acidic protons of each acid are neutralized. Which statement compares the volumes of NaOH required?

choices.t: They are equal, because the acids have the same concentration and volume.
H2SO4 needs twice as much, because each H2SO4 supplies two H⁺ to be neutralized.
HCl needs twice as much, because it is the stronger acid.
H2SO4 needs 1.5 times as much, because its second H⁺ is only partly ionized.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: A student titrates 20.0 mL of 0.150 M HBr (a strong acid) and, separately, 20.0 mL of 0.150 M HF (a weak acid, Ka = 6.8 × 10⁻⁴) with 0.100 M KOH. What volume of KOH is needed to reach the equivalence point in each titration?

choices.t: 30.0 mL for each acid
30.0 mL for HBr and less than 30.0 mL for HF
30.0 mL for HBr and more than 30.0 mL for HF
15.0 mL for each acid

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: In the reaction 2 Al(s) + Fe2O3(s) → Al2O3(s) + 2 Fe(s), which statement is correct?

choices.t: Al is the oxidizing agent because it is oxidized.
Fe2O3 is the reducing agent because the iron in it is reduced.
Fe2O3 is the oxidizing agent: each Fe goes from +3 to 0, and 6 electrons are transferred per Fe2O3.
Oxygen is oxidized, since it goes from -2 in Fe2O3 to 0 in Al2O3.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: In the reaction MnO4⁻ + 5 Fe²⁺ + 8 H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5 Fe³⁺ + 4 H2O, how many electrons does each MnO4⁻ gain, and which species is the reducing agent?

choices.t: 5 electrons; Fe²⁺ is the reducing agent
7 electrons; MnO4⁻ is the reducing agent
5 electrons; MnO4⁻ is the reducing agent
7 electrons; Fe²⁺ is the reducing agent

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: In the reaction CuO(s) + H2(g) → Cu(s) + H2O(g), which statement is correct?

choices.t: H2 is reduced and is the oxidizing agent.
Cu²⁺ in CuO is reduced, and H2 is the reducing agent.
Oxygen is reduced from -2 to 0.
Cu is oxidized from 0 to +2.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: In the reaction Zn(s) + 2 Ag⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + 2 Ag(s), how many electrons are transferred as the equation is written, and which species is the oxidizing agent?

choices.t: 2 electrons; Ag⁺ is the oxidizing agent
2 electrons; Zn is the oxidizing agent
1 electron; Ag⁺ is the oxidizing agent
4 electrons; Zn is the oxidizing agent

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: In the reaction 2 H2O2(aq) → 2 H2O(l) + O2(g), which statement about oxidation numbers is correct?

choices.t: Hydrogen is oxidized from +1 to 0.
Oxygen in H2O2 is -1; it is reduced to -2 in H2O and oxidized to 0 in O2, so H2O2 is both oxidized and reduced.
Oxygen is -2 in H2O2 and is only oxidized to 0 in O2, so H2O2 is only a reducing agent.
It is not a redox reaction, because only one reactant is present.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: In the reaction Cl2(g) + 2 NaOH(aq) → NaCl(aq) + NaOCl(aq) + H2O(l), which statement is correct?

choices.t: Chlorine is only reduced, because it forms the chloride ion.
Sodium is oxidized, because it appears in both products.
Oxygen is oxidized, because it goes from -2 in OH⁻ to -1 in NaOCl.
Chlorine is both oxidized and reduced, going from 0 in Cl2 to -1 in NaCl and +1 in NaOCl.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: In aqueous solution, copper(I) ions react according to 2 Cu⁺(aq) → Cu(s) + Cu²⁺(aq). Which statement is correct?

choices.t: It is not a redox reaction, because Cu appears on both sides of the equation.
Cu⁺ is only reduced, because copper metal forms.
Two electrons are transferred from each Cu⁺ ion to a neighboring ion.
One Cu⁺ is oxidized to Cu²⁺ and the other is reduced to Cu, so Cu⁺ is both the oxidizing and the reducing agent, with 1 electron transferred.

subject: AP Chemistry
stem: In the reaction 3 NO2(g) + H2O(l) → 2 HNO3(aq) + NO(g), which statement is correct?

choices.t: Nitrogen is only oxidized, because HNO3 has more oxygen than NO2.
Oxygen is reduced because it is -2 in NO2 and in NO.
Nitrogen is +4 in NO2, is oxidized to +5 in HNO3 and is reduced to +2 in NO, so NO2 is both oxidized and reduced.
Hydrogen is oxidized because it forms HNO3.
